title: CTCF-anchored chromatin loop dynamics during human meiosis.
authors: Kaiser, Vera B; Semple, Colin A
one_liner_zh: 该文用机器学习预测减数分裂中CTCF锚定染色质环动态，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作但聚焦染色质结构而非TF-DNA结合机制，方法为预测而非三维互作建模，相关性有限。
abstract: BACKGROUND: During meiosis, the mammalian genome is organised within chromatin loops, which facilitate synapsis, crossing over and chromosome segregation, setting the stage for recombination events and the generation of genetic diversity. Chromatin looping is thought to play a major role in the establishment of cross overs during prophase I of meiosis, in diploid early primary spermatocytes. However, chromatin conformation dynamics during human meiosis are difficult to study experimentally, due to the transience of each cell division and the difficulty of obtaining stage-resolved cell populations. Here, we employed a machine learning framework trained on single cell ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data to predict CTCF-anchored looping during spermatogenesis, including cell types at different stages of meiosis. RESULTS: We find dramatic changes in genome-wide looping patterns throughout meiosis: compared to pre-and-post meiotic germline cell types, loops in meiotic early primary spermatocytes are more abundant, more variable between individual cells, and more evenly spread throughout the genome. In preparation for the first meiotic division, loops also include longer stretches of DNA, encompassing more than half of the total genome. These loop structures then influence the rate of recombination initiation and resolution as cross overs. In contrast, in later mature sperm stages, we find evidence of genome compaction, with loops being confined to the telomeric ends of the chromosomes. CONCLUSION: Overall, we find that chromatin loops do not orchestrate the gene expression dynamics seen during spermatogenesis, but loops do play important roles in recombination, influencing the positions of DNA breakage and cross over events.
abstract_zh: 背景：在减数分裂过程中，哺乳动物基因组被组织在染色质环（chromatin loops）内，这些环促进联会、交叉和染色体分离，为重组事件和遗传多样性的产生奠定基础。染色质环被认为在减数分裂前期I的二倍体早期初级精母细胞中，对交叉的建立起主要作用。然而，由于每次细胞分裂的短暂性以及获取阶段分辨细胞群的困难，人类减数分裂期间的染色质构象动态难以通过实验研究。在此，我们采用了一种基于单细胞ATAC-seq和RNA-seq数据训练的机器学习框架，来预测精子发生过程中的CTCF锚定环，包括减数分裂不同阶段的细胞类型。结果：我们发现整个减数分裂过程中，全基因组环模式的显著变化：与减数分裂前和减数分裂后的生殖系细胞类型相比，减数分裂早期初级精母细胞中的环更丰富、在单个细胞间变异更大，并且更均匀地分布在整个基因组中。为第一次减数分裂做准备时，环还包含更长的DNA片段，覆盖总基因组的一半以上。这些环结构随后影响重组起始和交叉解决的速度。相反，在后期成熟精子阶段，我们发现了基因组压缩的证据，环被限制在染色体的端粒末端。结论：总体而言，我们发现染色质环并不协调精子发生过程中观察到的基因表达动态，但环在重组中发挥重要作用，影响DNA断裂和交叉事件的位置。
